name: ADP
scope_notes: Covers ADP Workforce Now / ADP API Central / ADP Marketplace APIs. API Central is a paid add-on for client-built integrations; Marketplace data connectors are partner apps; most ADP developer guides are public PDFs, while developers.adp.com is a JS app and admin/audit docs were not publicly readable.

controls.name: Credential reset (API Central)
controls.what: Reset the project's client credentials at any time.

controls.name: Team Access Management
controls.what: Roles control who can view API credentials and manage certificates; admins can revoke portal access.

controls.name: Project APIs / use case (API discovery tool)
controls.what: A project's credentials reach only the APIs added to that project.
controls.setting: API Central portal > project > add APIs

controls.name: Mutual TLS certificate
controls.what: Every token and API request must present the registered X.509 certificate, so a leaked secret alone is not enough.
controls.setting: API Central / Self Service portal > Certificate

controls.name: Consent Manager - Deny
controls.what: Client admin denies an allowed app so it no longer has access to the organization's ADP data.

controls.name: Consent Manager - Allow/Deny pending request
controls.what: Marketplace apps get no client credentials until the client consents.

controls.name: Cancel subscription
controls.what: Cancelling the Marketplace subscription stops the app's API calls for that client.
controls.setting: ADP Marketplace > My Apps > Manage App > cancel subscription

controls.name: Shorter access token lifetime at registration
controls.what: A shorter token expiry can be requested during application registration.

controls.name: Project users role (API Central Members page)
controls.what: Only members assigned the Project users role can create projects and access API credentials; withholding the role blocks credential creation.

controls.name: Client consent before subscriber credentials are released
controls.what: The partner gets a client's Client ID and Secret only after that client consents to the partner solution.

controls_unknown: Whether a customer-configurable IP allowlist exists for API Central credentials (docs only say tokens 'may be' tied to an IP).
Whether credential reset or consent denial revokes already-issued access tokens immediately.
What audit/log records exist for credential creation, reset, token issuance and API calls, and how clients access them.
Whether API Central certificates can be revoked by the client before expiry.
Whether consumer-application-subscription-credentials.read returns the same or new secrets after re-consent.

credentials.name: API Central project client credentials (client ID/secret + mutual TLS certificate)

authentication.summary: Starting an API Central project generates a client ID and secret. The app posts them with grant_type=client_credentials to accounts.adp.com over mTLS using its ADP-signed certificate, then calls api.adp.com with the bearer token and the same certificate.

federation.details: No user sign-in is involved; docs do not discuss SSO or conditional access for API calls.

ip_restriction.boundary: ADP may tie tokens to the computing environment (e.g. IP) used at authorization; this is ADP-side, not a customer-configurable allowlist.

lifetime.summary: Access token 60 min; secret static until reset; certificate 2 years

renewal.summary: App requests a new token with the secret and certificate; certificate renewed via new CSR.

administration.summary: API Central portal: projects, credential reset, certificate management, Team Access Management roles (Project, Certificate, Member users).

sso.details: API Central projects are data connectors; the API actor is a client agent that is not authenticated as a user, so user SSO/MFA does not apply.

offboard.details: The API actor is a pre-assigned system (non-human) user, not the person who created the project.

inventory.details: API Central Projects page shows project cards; docs describe it as the projects you create, not an org-wide credential list.

expiry.ui: API Central > Certificate > Certificate management card shows expiration date; shorter token lifetime only by request at registration

token_format.notes: Access token is an opaque UUID-like string (example 27b16f3c-...); expires_in 3600.

anomaly_cues: New certificate requested/uploaded in API Central
New team member with Project user role

containment.steps: Reset project credentials in API Central; replace the certificate; remove portal members.

unknown: Any customer-visible API or audit log

credentials.name: Marketplace data connector client credentials (held by partner app)

authentication.summary: After a client buys a Marketplace app and consents, the partner retrieves that client's client ID/secret via consumer-application-subscription-credentials.read and uses client credentials over mTLS to call the client's APIs.

federation.details: Consent is given by a client user; API calls afterwards use client credentials with no user session.

ip_restriction.boundary: ADP may tie tokens to the IP used at authorization; no customer-configurable allowlist documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token 60 min; credentials last while consent and subscription are active

renewal.summary: Partner mints new tokens with stored client credentials.

administration.summary: Client admin controls access through Consent Manager (Allow/Deny) and Marketplace subscription cancellation.

sso.details: Data connector API actor is a client agent that is not authenticated as a user.

offboard.details: Credentials act as a system agent user created for the data connector, not a person.

inventory.details: Consent Manager (adpapps.adp.com/consent-manager) lists allowed and denied app consents; WFN lists each connector's System Agent User under Marketplace Data Connector Profile > Members.

expiry.ui: Request a shorter access-token lifetime from ADP at application registration (default 60 min)

usage.ui: (Partner) ADP Marketplace > profile > Developer > Integration Events; Show Filters, filter Event Type and date; User/Company column names the client

kill.ui: adpapps.adp.com/consent-manager > Allowed Consents > Deny > I'm Sure; and ADP Marketplace > My Apps > app tile cog > Manage App > cancel subscription

log_sources.name: Marketplace event logs
log_sources.notes: Referenced for subscription cancellation; access method and retention not documented.

lifecycle_events.notes: Shown in Marketplace event logs per partner checklist; exact event name not given.

anomaly_cues: Unknown apps in Consent Manager Allowed Consents

containment.steps: Deny the app in Consent Manager and cancel the Marketplace subscription.
containment.notes: ADP validates consent before processing API calls, so denial should block calls; immediate effect on live tokens not stated.

unknown: Client-visible log of partner API calls

credentials.name: Marketplace Partner API / Data Connector credentials (partner-level)

authentication.summary: The partner's own client ID/secret from the Self Service portal, used with the partner mTLS certificate to get a token that can read client credentials for every consented subscriber.

federation.details: Held by the partner, not by the customer tenant.

ip_restriction.boundary: ADP may tie tokens to the IP used at authorization; no allowlist documented for partner or client.

administration.summary: Managed by the partner in the ADP Self Service portal; scopes added by ADP ticket. The customer's only lever is consent/subscription.

sso.details: Partner-level credentials authenticate an application, with no end-user authentication.

offboard.details: ADP issues one set of credentials per application, not per user.

inventory.details: The partner sees its projects and credentials in the Partner Self Service Portal; the subscribing client has no view of partner-level credentials.

inventory.ui: (Partner) Self Service Portal > Projects > {project} > Development API Credentials

expiry.ui: (Partner) Self Service Portal > Certificate > Request Certificate > Check Status > note Expiration Date; token lifetime per registration (default 60 min)

kill.ui: (Client) adpapps.adp.com/consent-manager > Allowed Consents > Deny > I'm Sure

anomaly_cues: Partner credential compromise exposes every consented client; customers cannot see it directly

containment.steps: Customer: deny consent / cancel subscription. Partner: reset credentials in Self Service portal.
containment.notes: Client side: revoking consent in Consent Manager turns the integration off instantly. Partner credential reset timing not documented.

calls.reveals: Client ID and secret for a consented subscriber (by OOID)
